# Build this repo's vsim inside the Dockerfile's env-stage container image.

set -euo pipefail

# Container runtime: prefer podman, fall back to docker.
if command -v podman >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=podman
elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RUNTIME=docker
else
  echo "error: need podman or docker on PATH" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/Dockerfile" ]]; then
  echo "error: missing $ROOT/Dockerfile" >&2
  exit 1

if [[ ! -f "$ROOT/external/fmt/CMakeLists.txt" ]]; then
  echo "error: submodules not initialized - run:" >&2
  echo "  git submodule update --init --recursive" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$ROOT"

"$RUNTIME" build --target env -t vsim-env:latest .
"$RUNTIME" run --rm \
  -v "$ROOT:/work" \

Errors can be synchronous or asynchronous. Synchronous errors are reported in the upstream re-
sponse of an upstream request, while asynchronous errors are reported through l3c_err_int.
Asynchronous errors include:
• A CCTL operation encounters uncorrectable RAM errors (RAM error).
• A CCTL operation encounters bus errors (Bus error).
• A CCTL operation probes the D-Cache when D-Cache coherency is disabled (Probe error).
• An L3 eviction encounters uncorrectable RAM errors or bus errors.
• The D-Cache writes back a line not in the L3-Cache (Release error).
• The L3-Cache sends an L3 request to write back a line, and the response has bus errors (Bus error).
When an asynchronous error occurs, the Asynchronous Error Register and Error Register are updated.
The error status can be cleared by writing any value to the corresponding ﬁeld in the Asynchronous
Error Register.
Non-Repairable Soft Faults
A non-repairable soft fault is resolved differently depending on which cache RAM detects the error.
When an asynchronous non-repairable soft fault is detected in the tag RAM or data RAM, the error
is reported in the Error Register with the ERRTYPE ﬁeld set to 0x0, and the l3c_err_int interrupt
pin is asserted.
If the error is detected in the snoop ﬁlter, the snoop ﬁlter enters broadcast mode by deasserting the
SFEN bit in the Control Register 1. The error is also reported in the Error Register with the ERRTYPE
ﬁeld set to 0x0, and the l3c_err_int interrupt pin is asserted. To handle this error, software should
read the Error Register, resolve, and acknowledge the error by writing to the Asynchronous Error
Register. Then, re-enable the snoop ﬁlter as described in the Section 15.4.
Hard Faults
If a cache error is found consecutively at the same cache location, it is classiﬁed a hard fault. Hard
fault handling is the same as for a non-repairable soft fault, except it is reported in the Error Register
with the ERRTYPE ﬁeld set to 0x3.

the shared cache. In contrast, L3-Cache CCTL commands can continue to operate on the L3-Cache.

1	/* Why timing-config transport matters: the cache-enable state.
2	 *
3	 * The andesim runtime's crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches by writing
4	 * mcache_ctl (0x7CA) at boot. On hybrid that write runs on QEMU, which
5	 * models no caches -- the ONLY reason the vsim ROI runs cached is that
6	 * the handoff transports the written mcache_ctl value and restores it
7	 * before the ROI resumes. This demo makes that visible as a number:
8	 *
9	 *   cache_on.elf   the default program: crt0's enable is transported,
10	 *                  the ROI runs WITH L1 caches -- what this program
11	 *                  would do on real silicon.
12	 *   cache_off.elf  same source, -DCACHE_OFF: the program clears
13	 *                  mcache_ctl.IC_EN|DC_EN (bits 0|1) before the ROI,
14	 *                  so the transported value disables the caches and
15	 *                  the same kernel runs UNCACHED -- every instruction
16	 *                  fetch and data access goes out to DRAM.
17	 *
18	 * The gap between the two figures is what the transport buys; without
19	 * it, EVERY hybrid window would measure like cache_off (the engine's
20	 * reset default is caches-disabled). It is also a write-mask demo: a
21	 * config CSR is restored only because the program (crt0 or the
22	 * CACHE_OFF line) actually wrote it.
23	 *
24	 * The ROI is a pure kernel -- PASSES sweeps over a 4 KB volatile array,
25	 * no I/O inside the window. The checksum verdict (CACHE_OK) prints
26	 * after the ROI, so it appears on fast and cycle only; on hybrid the
27	 * output is just the cycle figure, compared by check.sh.
28	 *

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-asserting harness for the cache demo: the transported cache-enable
# state must be worth a multiple in the hybrid cycle figure. Same pattern as
# demo/memsize/check.sh.
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
ENG=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}
RATIO_MIN=${RATIO_MIN:-2}   # uncached must cost > RATIO_MIN x cached

pass=0 fail=0
# assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD...
assert() {
  local desc=$1 want_rc=$2 want_re=$3; shift 3
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] && grep -qiE "$want_re" <<<"$out"; then
    printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$desc"; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] %s\n       rc=%s (want %s), no /%s/ in:\n       %s\n' \
      "$desc" "$rc" "$want_rc" "$want_re" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

# run_cycles CMD... -> echoes the N of "[andesim] N cycles", empty on failure
run_cycles() {
  local out
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1) || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; return 1; }
  sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1
}

echo "--- both builds are functionally sound (fast; QEMU has no caches) ---"
assert "fast cache_on:  CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_on.elf
assert "fast cache_off: CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_off.elf

echo "--- the same ROI, hybrid, cached vs uncached ---"
on=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_on.elf)
off=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_off.elf)

if [ -z "$on" ] || [ -z "$off" ]; then
  echo "[FAIL] hybrid figure missing (on='$on' off='$off')"; fail=$((fail+1))
else
  ratio=$(awk -v a="$off" -v b="$on" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", a/b}')
  printf 'cached   (crt0 enable transported): %8s cycles\n' "$on"
  printf 'uncached (program cleared IC|DC):   %8s cycles\n' "$off"
  printf 'ratio: %sx (must be > %sx)\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
  if [ "$off" -gt $((RATIO_MIN * on)) ]; then
    printf '[PASS] cache-enable transport is worth %sx on this kernel\n' "$ratio"
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] uncached/cached ratio %sx did not clear %sx\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

/* andesim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --mode fast, --mode cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_H
#define ANDESIM_ROI_H

static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDESIM_ROI_H */

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-asserting harness for the cache demo: the transported cache-enable
# state must be worth a multiple in the hybrid cycle figure. Same pattern as
# demo/memsize/check.sh.
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
ENG=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}
RATIO_MIN=${RATIO_MIN:-2}   # uncached must cost > RATIO_MIN x cached

pass=0 fail=0
# assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD...
assert() {
  local desc=$1 want_rc=$2 want_re=$3; shift 3
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] && grep -qiE "$want_re" <<<"$out"; then
    printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$desc"; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] %s\n       rc=%s (want %s), no /%s/ in:\n       %s\n' \
      "$desc" "$rc" "$want_rc" "$want_re" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

# run_cycles CMD... -> echoes the N of "[andesim] N cycles", empty on failure
run_cycles() {
  local out
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1) || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; return 1; }
  sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1
}

echo "--- both builds are functionally sound (fast; QEMU has no caches) ---"
assert "fast cache_on:  CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_on.elf
assert "fast cache_off: CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_off.elf

echo "--- the same ROI, hybrid, cached vs uncached ---"
on=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_on.elf)
off=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_off.elf)

if [ -z "$on" ] || [ -z "$off" ]; then
  echo "[FAIL] hybrid figure missing (on='$on' off='$off')"; fail=$((fail+1))
else
  ratio=$(awk -v a="$off" -v b="$on" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", a/b}')
  printf 'cached   (crt0 enable transported): %8s cycles\n' "$on"
  printf 'uncached (program cleared IC|DC):   %8s cycles\n' "$off"
  printf 'ratio: %sx (must be > %sx)\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
  if [ "$off" -gt $((RATIO_MIN * on)) ]; then
    printf '[PASS] cache-enable transport is worth %sx on this kernel\n' "$ratio"
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] uncached/cached ratio %sx did not clear %sx\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

# Register a header-only hybrid doctest: build it (vsim_add_test marks it
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL), expose the shared ABI headers from the andesim_abi
# submodule (external/andesim_abi/hybrid), and wire it into the `check`
# target. The include path is inert for the handful of tests that do not
# pull in state_abi.h.
function(hybrid_add_test name source)
  vsim_add_test(${name} ${source})
  target_include_directories(${name} PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/andesim_abi")
  add_dependencies(check ${name})
